chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: The Manassas festival recordings and Fat Cat
summary: She sang there because Cliff was going; she was angry about unknowing recording; various Fat Cat albums and liner mix-ups.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Alright. And you're saying of course, that you had done the 1966 Manassas Jazz Festival.
Oh yes.
And you said that came out of your association with Tom Gwaltney.

Well I think that that was before I did Tommy - no, it was afterwards. Cliff knew Johnson McCree, you know, these people would come into Ryan's where Cliff was working and I guess he knew these people over a period of years. And of course Cliff is supposed to have been born down that way, Culpepper, Virginia, and so Fat Cat, Johnson McCree got together with Cliff and they had a Jazz Festival. Well, they had them every year. They were using local guys in the beginning.
So that wasn't the first on in '56?

I don't think so. So Cliff was going down so Fat Cat asked me to sing and I did. Well, you know Fat Cat and Tommy and the Mayor of Arlington, Virginia were the co-owners of Blue's Alley. So that was the association there. And of course Fat Cat taped the
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Okay, and that has five of your songs on it.
Yeah.
Okay, now did you tell me before that you didn't know that that was being recorded at the time?
No I didn't.
Okay, in retrospect your record came out.
Oh well, in the beginning I was a little angry because we weren't informed, you know.
You didn't have a contract with him in which . . .

No, no. Not when you go down there to do that. I've done the Jazz Festival since that time and he let's you know it's going to be recorded. In fact, we did one concert down there, and you know Fat Cat calls himself 'the poor man's Big Gibson'. He does the same type thing Big Gibson does. He brings alot of musicians down there too. But really on a smaller scale. And on this particular occasion I - you never know which
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

group you're going to be singing with. You know, they mix it up. On this particular occasion I sang some things with Bobby Hackett and Vic Dickerson. So I happened to have been up in Boston after that, this was after I started back really singing and doing these things, and Bobby Hackett was on the gig and he came up with this album, Fat Cat had put out this album, you know, Bobby Hackett, Vic Dickerson and Maxine Sullivan which I don't guess Bobby knew about or Dick or I. It's one of those things you know, they taped it. But now everything is above board.
So that first festival was in May of '56, I believe. And all the others have been in December, the subsequent ones you've appeared on.
Yeah.
That's what made me thing that was the first.
No, you know, I'm not sure. Some of the things on Fat Cat's albums, they are not all recorded at the same time. What he does is he takes a little bit of this and that and he puts it together.
Yeah.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I do know that if we're talking about the one in which Bob Scushon is on . . .
Yes.

Well that was done in Manassas. But there's another album that he put out called Maxine Sullivan; Queen of Song, and that is from different sessions we did, one of which was done in, I believe, in Norfork. They had a very big festival down there which wasn't the Manassas Jazz Festival at all. It was just another festival. I remember having done that, and I believe that that's the one in which Felix Grant introduces me. So that wasn't recorded in Manassas at all. That was recorded in Norfork.
Okay, I don't have that 'Queen Of Song' information with me here.
You wouldn't know that by the liner notes on the album.
Yeah. What you're saying is when Felix gives the introduction, that was actually taken off . . .
Yeah.
Okay.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And on that engagement they had quite a few, they had Toots Thielmans down there, and of course Tommy and his group and Cliff, and I believe maybe Marian and Jimmy McPartland and some of the guys.
Has that been enjoyable sort of engagements for you doing that festival?

Oh yeah, well you always have fun. It's a fun thing. I imagine Fat has allot of material down there. Well, you know, there's quite a bit of activity in the South especially when it comes to traditional jazz. And allot of fans in the South who really dig these things and there's a big membership of traditional jazz fans around there. And I believe that this is where the bulk of the distribution comes in. And they distribute by means of what they call membership. They have a mailing list and they publish their latest acquisitions along with some of the older stuff that they have and they have quite an interest in the South, but it's mainly for traditional jazz.
